title: Pound to Rise Further if May Secures Support for Brexit Plan, Credit Suisse Says
description: Jul.09 -- Shahab Jalinoos, global head of FX trading strategy at Credit Suisse, discusses the outlook for the pound as U.K. Prime Minister Theresa May moved fast to contain a crisis in her government after her chief Brexit negotiator quit. He speaks on "Bloomberg Daybreak: Americas" alongside Lindsey Bell, investment strategist at CFRA.

asr.full_text: Take a look at Sterling's reaction. Up, but not that much. What was your take on this? Well, I think it makes sense that Sterling is performing well because ultimately this is a step towards a softer Brexit. That's what really matters. But should it be performing better? Well, it probably will in the end. I think what we need to see first is May try to sell the new policy to the conservative backbench MPs and others. Get through that phase and see that there isn't really going to be an attempt to bring down the government at this point. Once we have some more clarity on that, then I think you will see the pound strengthen further from here. Because we do have a lot of short positions in the market. And if you come inside the Bloomberg, you can see. So this is a net positioning for sterling. And you can see the net shorts are those blue bars. And the white line is where we are for the pound spot. What kind of snapback may we see? What kind of levels are you looking at if this winds up progressing and they get through the 1922 and it gets through the white paper later on this week? Well, I'm looking mostly at euro sterling. I think that's a purer way of looking at the pound than the pound against the dollar. I think 87.50 is a very important level. If we can get to that level and push below that, then I think that we'll be in new territory in a sense. It may take a while, though, as I said, because there will be, at least for the next couple of weeks,. Some sense that there could be an attempt to bring down the government lingering in the background. Once we see that that's not really going to happen, I think we'll see the good move begin. So you made the point earlier, like, who's going to ever want that job at the end of the day? You might not like Theresa May, but you need someone there who's not you. So, Lindsay Bell, how do you wind up looking at U.K. assets right now in an asset allocation portfolio? For asset allocation, we see in Europe in general the political stance, the concern there really as an issue. And so because of that, while the valuations are pretty good and right now earnings growth over there is expected to be pretty decent, 8.5% in 2019 versus 10% S&P 500, we're a little more cautious. So we do recommend that our clients overweight domestic equities. So what's the next key thing that you're looking forward to once we get past this? Is her government going to stay, Shahab? It's going to be the Bank of England. In August, the Bank of England has another meeting. And the market's beginning to think about the possibility of a rate hike. And I think that's very important here because despite all this noise,. Clearly the economy has not performed too badly if we're still considering a rate hike at this point in time. And once that becomes the center focus for the market and the politics dies down a bit,. Then I think the pound gets a back run from that as well. And obviously the backdrop has to do with the dollar, which leads me to sort of what. To expect in earnings season. For the dollar perspective, Shahab, have we peaked out or is there more upside? Well I think in the medium term, you know, the bets, all bets are open still in terms. Of where the dollar goes. Near term I think we have probably peaked out for now. There's a couple of things that have changed. China appears to have given many signals to the market that maybe the 670 level in dollar. CNH was enough for now. And I think the fact that dollar China is stabilizing, dollar CNH is stabilized is important. You've also seen the Mexican peso trade quite well in the aftermath of the Mexican election. So some of the key currencies the market was concerned about are now performing in a relatively. Stable fashion. You also have now the end of the summer coming up, maybe the European summer holidays, a. Time when normally volatility in FX markets subside and the carry currencies do well. And that's good for emerging markets as well. So I think when you put these things together,. It suggests that the dollar may have had a local peak for now.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is presented as Bloomberg financial-news analysis of a Credit Suisse FX strategist's discussion of the pound outlook amid Brexit-related political uncertainty. The discussion covers sterling performance, possible further pound strength, asset allocation, and domestic-equity positioning as conditional market views. The studio-news setting, market charts, and political-finance headlines contextualize the currency figures as reporting and analysis rather than a deceptive solicitation.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The primary subject is financial news and market analysis: the segment discusses the pound's outlook, sterling positioning, asset allocation and the dollar in relation to Brexit and political developments. The supplied evidence does not show a reward flow, solicitation, credential request or paid earning guidance.
